advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Broaden the static scan (or document its limit) so a live-Jira test gating on acli via a module-level helper without a group mark is still flagged.
evidence: tests/unit/test_live_jira_xdist_confinement.py:59: `if _is_acli_on_path_probe(node) and not _carries_group(node.decorator_list):` — per-function detection requires the which("acli") Call node inside the function body

tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py:135-141: the live-env gate lives in the module-level helper `_live_env_available()` (calls `which("acli")`), not in any test function body — a test written this way relies solely on the module pytestmark check to be caught
ABSENCE: no case handles a live test that reaches acli through a helper call while lacking both a module pytestmark group and a per-function mark; such a test passes the scan silently
advisory.finding: The static policy scan _unconfined_live_jira_tests() only flags a live-Jira test when the which("acli") probe appears lexically inside the test function's own AST subtree (or the module has a group pytestmark). A test that gates on live Jira via a module-level helper (e.g. the _live_env_available()/_requires_live pattern used by tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py) but has neither a module-level xdist_group pytestmark nor a per-function xdist_group mark would NOT be flagged, defeating the guard whose stated purpose is to catch exactly the class of omission that shipped test_reconcile_dry_run_against_live_jira without a mark.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a subprocess guard case for `-n 2 --dist load` (and a bare `-n 2` with no `--dist`) asserting collection is rejected when live creds are present.
evidence: Commit message: `an ad-hoc \`pytest -n auto\` gets --dist load` — the default-scheduler path is the named defect but no test passes `--dist load` or an `-n` with no `--dist`.
Predicate under test rejects via `if dist == "loadgroup": return None` (tests/_live_jira_confinement.py:84), so `load` should be rejected too, but nothing asserts it.
advisory.finding: No test exercises the guard under `--dist load` (xdist's default) or under a bare `-n 2` with no `--dist` flag (which resolves to `load`). The subprocess guards only cover `--dist worksteal` (rejected) and `--dist loadgroup` (accepted). The commit message and the module docstring both identify the default `load` scheduler — hit by an ad-hoc `pytest -n auto` — as the primary gap (gap #1), yet the rejection path is only proven for `worksteal`. A regression that special-cased the predicate to only reject `worksteal` (e.g. `dist == 'worksteal'` instead of `dist != 'loadgroup'`) would pass all tests while leaving the default-scheduler scatter unguarded.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `test_parallel_with_default_load_scheduler_is_rejected` and `test_parallel_without_explicit_dist_is_rejected` calling `_collect(tmp_path, "-n", "2", "--dist", "load", live_env=True)` and `_collect(tmp_path, "-n", "2", live_env=True)` respectively, both asserting `cp.returncode != 0` and the guard message in output.

tests/_live_jira_confinement.py:78: `if not isinstance(numprocesses, int) or isinstance(numprocesses, bool): return None` — the bool sub-branch cannot be produced by a real `-n` CLI value, so subprocess tests cannot cover it.
tests/_live_jira_confinement.py:58: `names = [*marker.args, marker.kwargs.get("name")]` — only positional `xdist_group("...")` is used in the repo, leaving the kwargs branch untested.
advisory.finding: The pure predicate `unconfined_live_jira_reason` and `live_jira_credentials_available` have no direct unit test, despite the module docstring explicitly justifying its extraction as a PURE predicate 'so it is directly callable and testable without spawning pytest.' Two branches are unreachable via the subprocess route and thus wholly untested: the `isinstance(numprocesses, bool)` guard (tests/_live_jira_confinement.py:78 — you cannot pass `-n True` on a command line), and the `marker.kwargs.get("name")` branch in `_grouped_node_ids` (line 58 — the group is only ever applied positionally in the repo, so the `xdist_group(name=...)` keyword form is never exercised).
advisory.suggested_fix: Add table-driven unit tests constructing a fake `config` (with `getoption` returning bool/int) and fake items (marker via kwargs `name=`), asserting `unconfined_live_jira_reason` returns None for the bool case and a message for the keyword-marked group case; monkeypatch env + `shutil.which` for `live_jira_credentials_available`.
